newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-DE GLANVILLE DEFENDS ROWELL AFTER ENGLAND DEFEAT.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-DE GLANVILLE DEFENDS ROWELL AFTER ENGLAND DEFEAT.

text.p: England captain Phil de Glanville made a spirited defence of coach Jack Rowell after the Triple Crown winners sank to a crushing 25-6 defeat against Australia on Saturday in what could be Rowell's last match in charge.
The Wallabies ran in four tries without reply at the Sydney Football Stadium at the end of a week dominated by rumours that Rowell's three-year tenure as England coach is about to end.

De Glanville, one of only three England players on duty who did not feature in the recent British Lions series win against South Africa, said the rumours had done nothing for the reputation of the English Rugby Union (RFU).
"He (Rowell) has done a good job and the players respect him," De Glanville told reporters after the match.
"Certainly what's gone on this week has not been good for the squad and certainly not good for the reputation of the game and the RFU. We shall have to see what happens."
The build-up to Saturday's game was disrupted by media reports in London suggesting the RFU had approached Auckland's New Zealand coach Graham Henry about taking over the England job for next season.
Asked how confident he was of staying on, Rowell, whose contract expires next month, said: "I don't think about it," before asking reporters not to pose any further questions on the subject.

Australia dominated for virtually the whole match on Saturday but, despite their overwhelming superiority, they led only 8-6 early in the second half because of some poor finishing and inaccurate kicking.
Three late tries from winger Ben Tune, scrum-half George Gregan and fly-half Tim Horan added some realism to the scoreline as the tired English defence finally began to miss some tackles.
It was Horan's first try since his switch from the centres by Wallaby coach Greg Smith this season.
And the margin of victory would have been even greater but for a mediocre kicking display by Australia captain and lock John Eales, who missed one conversion and three penalty attempts.
Australia have beaten England in all eight meetings on home soil since 1963 and the latest victory exacted some belated revenge for their defeat in a World Cup quarter-final two years ago.
The visitors relied on the accurate kicking of fly-half Mike Catt, who landed a penalty and a drop goal either side of half-time.
Full-back Matt Burke, who missed Australia's last three test matches because of a groin strain, made a telling impact on his return by scoring the opening try after 12 minutes.
Horan began the move with a cut-out pass to winger Joe Roff, who came into the line to find a gap in the centres before releasing Burke into the open.
Burke, Australia's regular goal-kicker, added to his points tally with one conversion after taking from Eales in the second half.
"We did some good things in the second half and it was a tough match because England defended very well," Australia coach Greg Smith said.
"We had the territorial advantage but we did not score as many tries as we should have. We did not synchronise our play all that well at times."
